events.title: Asian Shares Mixed In Choppy Trade
events.description: Asian stocks ended mixed on Friday due to concerns over technology valuations and escalating Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.

events.title: UK Retail Sales Fall More Than Forecast
events.description: UK retail sales declined more than expected in September as warm weather weighed on clothing and supermarket sales, data released by the Office for National Statistics showed on Friday. Retail sales decreased 0.4 percent in September, reversing a rise of 0.7 percent in August and exceeded economists' forecast of a 0.1 percent fall.

events.title: NZ Dollar Rises Against Majors
events.description: The New Zealand dollar strengthened against other major currencies in the Asian session on Friday.

events.title: European Shares Set To Extend Losses Amid AI Worries, Mideast Tensions
events.description: European stocks are seen opening lower on Friday after U.S. tech shares sold off overnight on concerns over the faltering global AI trade.

events.title: Indian Shares Give Up Early Gains
events.description: Indian shares were moving lower on Friday, giving up early gains on concerns over rising oil prices following Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure and Red Sea ports.

events.title: Australian Market Trims Early Losses In Mid-market
events.description: The Australian stock market is trimming its early losses in mid-market moves on Friday, but extending the losses in the previous session, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 is falling well below the 8,800 level, with weakness in across most sectors led by mining and technology stocks. Financial stocks were the only bright spot.

events.title: Asian Markets Trade Mostly Lower
events.description: Asian stock markets are trading mostly lower on Friday, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight, on a renewed spike in crude oil prices amid the re-escalation of tensions in the Middle East. Technology and semiconductor stocks also took a hit amid renewed concerns about debt-fueled AI infrastructure spending, with concerns about AI seeming to shift on a daily basis.

events.title: Indian Shares Seen Higher At Open After Recent Losses
events.description: Indian shares are seen opening higher on Friday, with information technology stocks likely to be in the spotlight after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeted 6.7 percent to its lowest closing level in almost three months overnight following disappointing earnings from Meta Platforms and Tesla, and amid lingering concerns over rising AI-related spending.

events.title: Japanese Market Sharply Lower
events.description: The Japanese market is trading sharply lower on Friday, extending the losses in the previous session, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is falling below the 61,950 level, with weakness in across most sectors led by technology and financial stocks.

events.title: Indonesia Stock Market: Resistance Expected At 5,400 Points
events.description: The Indonesia stock market has finished higher in three straight sessions, adding more than 390 points or 7.6 percent in that span. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just beneath the 5,390-point plateau although the rally may stall on Friday.

events.title: Lower Open Predicted For Hong Kong Stock Market
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market has finished lower in three straight sessions, retreating more than 1,450 points or 4.3 percent along the way. The Hang Seng now sits just above the 22,930-point plateau and it's got another poor lead for Friday's trade.

events.title: Australian Market Modestly Lower
events.description: The Australian stock market is trading modestly lower on Friday, extending the losses in the previous session, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 is falling below the 8,800 level, with weakness in across most sectors led by mining and technology stocks. Financial stocks were the only bright spot.

events.title: China Stock Market Tipped To Open In The Red On Friday
events.description: The China stock market has finished lower in back-to-back sessions, slumping more than 75 points or 2.1 percent along the way. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,660-point plateau and it's looking at another soft start again on Friday.
